title: Impact of Welfare Eligibility on Labor Supply

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) is the appropriate method since welfare eligibility is determined by a strict income threshold (running variable). The key assumption is that individuals cannot precisely manipulate their income around the cutoff, ensuring quasi-random assignment of treatment status near the threshold. This creates a sharp discontinuity where crossing the income threshold determines welfare eligibility.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s92_data.csv")

# Examine the data structure
print("Data summary:")
print(summary(data))

# Determine the cutoff (threshold where treatment changes)
cutoff <- 0.5  # Assuming normalized threshold at 0.5

# Center the running variable around the cutoff
data$running_var_centered <- data$running_var - cutoff

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = cutoff)

# Print main results
print("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===")
print(paste("Treatment Effect (Local Average Treatment Effect):", round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(rdd_result$se[1], 4)))
print(paste("95% Confidence Interval: [", round(rdd_result$ci[1,1], 4), ", ", round(rdd_result$ci[1,2], 4), "]"))
print(paste("P-value:", round(rdd_result$pv[1], 4)))
print(paste("Bandwidth used:", round(rdd_result$bws[1], 4)))
print(paste("Number of observations:", rdd_result$N[1] + rdd_result$N[2]))

# Robustness checks

# 1. Alternative bandwidth
rdd_half_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = cutoff, h = rdd_result$bws[1] * 0.5)
rdd_double_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = cutoff, h = rdd_result$bws[1] * 2)

print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")
print(paste("Half bandwidth - Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_half_bw$coef[1], 4), 
            "SE:", round(rdd_half_bw$se[1], 4)))
print(paste("Double bandwidth - Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_double_bw$coef[1], 4), 
            "SE:", round(rdd_double_bw$se[1], 4)))

# 2. Different polynomial orders
rdd_p2 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 2)
print(paste("Quadratic polynomial - Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_p2$coef[1], 4), 
            "SE:", round(rdd_p2$se[1], 4)))

# 3. Manipulation test (McCrary density test)
density_test <- rddensity(data$running_var, c = cutoff)
print(paste("\nMcCrary Density Test p-value:", round(density_test$test$p_jk, 4)))
print("(High p-value suggests no manipulation)")

# 4. Balance test on pre-treatment characteristics (if available)
# Using running_var as a placebo outcome
balance_test <- rdrobust(y = data$running_var, x = data$running_var, c = cutoff)
print(paste("Balance test p-value:", round(balance_test$pv[1], 4)))

# Create visualization
rdplot_result <- rdplot(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = cutoff, 
                       title = "RDD: Welfare Eligibility Impact on Labor Supply",
                       x.label = "Income (Running Variable)", 
                       y.label = "Hours Worked")

print("\n=== FINAL RESULT ===")
print(paste("The estimated causal effect of welfare eligibility on labor supply is:", 
            round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "hours"))
if(rdd_result$pv[1] < 0.05) {
  print("This effect is statistically significant at the 5% level.")
} else {
  print("This effect is not statistically significant at the 5% level.")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative coefficient (approximately -0.3 to -0.7 hours), indicating that welfare eligibility reduces labor supply. This aligns with economic theory suggesting that welfare benefits create work disincentives through income and substitution effects - individuals may reduce work hours when eligible for benefits since they have an alternative income source and face implicit high marginal tax rates when earning above the threshold. The magnitude should be economically meaningful but not extremely large, as most welfare programs are designed to avoid creating severe work disincentives.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Examine changes in labor supply around the income threshold for welfare eligibility.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Crossing the income threshold for welfare eligibility results in a reduction in labor supply.
